definitions.explanation: The imaginary line at roughly 180° longitude that marks where the calendar date changes. Almost always appears in the full form {日付変更線|ひづけへんこうせん}; the short form is used only after the full term has been established.

examples.japanese: {日付|ひづけ}{変更線|へんこうせん}を{越|こ}えた。
examples.english: We crossed the International Date Line.

examples.japanese: {変更線|へんこうせん}を{西|にし}に{越|こ}えると{日付|ひづけ}が{進|すす}む。
examples.english: Crossing the date line going west moves the date forward.

examples.japanese: {太平洋|たいへいよう}{上空|じょうくう}で{日付|ひづけ}{変更線|へんこうせん}を{通過|つうか}し、カレンダーが{一日|いちにち}{戻|もど}った。
examples.english: We passed the International Date Line over the Pacific and the calendar went back one day.

notes:
Compound of {変更|へんこう} (change) + {線|せん} (line). The standalone word is uncommon; the standard term is {日付|ひづけ}{変更線|へんこうせん} (date-change line).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {日付|ひづけ}{変更線|へんこうせん}: International Date Line (full term)
- {変更線|へんこうせん}を{越|こ}える: to cross the date line
- {変更線|へんこうせん}を{通過|つうか}する: to pass over the date line

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {経度|けいど}: longitude — the angular measure, not the dateline itself
- {時差|じさ}: time difference — between time zones, related but distinct concept
